entries.title: go.mod text-attribute recurrence is now CI-guarded, but the module-path resolvability smoke test the finding also asked for is still missing
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `ai-shared-lib/.github/workflows/ci.yml`, step "go.mod is a text git attribute (SC-RESOLVE)" (around line 71-84). Also `ai-shared-lib/.gitattributes` (`go.mod text -filter` override, lines ~9-11 under the "Go module manifest/checksum" comment block).

**Symptom.** None today for the LFS/text-attribute half — that half is fixed and guarded. The still-open half: nothing in CI builds any module from its module-path form (`go get`/`go build <module-path>`), so an unresolvable bare module path (the other half of the original defect) can still ship undetected.

**Reproduction.** 1. Read `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 71-84: a required job step walks every tracked `*go.mod` with `git ls-files -z -- '*go.mod'` and fails if `git check-attr text` does not report `set`. This guard exists and runs on every push/PR. 2. Search the same workflow file and `ci-go.yml` for any step invoking `go build`/`go get` against a module-path (rather than a relative `-C`/working-directory path): none exists. 3. `.gitattributes` already carries the override `go.mod text -filter` layered after the generic `*.mod filter=lfs ...` rule, confirming the LFS-pointer half of the original defect is fixed at the attribute level, independent of the CI check.

**Root cause.** The bare-unqualified-module-path defect (the other half of this finding) has no guard because CI never resolves a module by its declared path — established by absence, not by a citation of the defect recurring.

**Proposed fix.** Add a smoke-test step (e.g. in `ci-go.yml` or a new job) that runs `go build <module-path>/...` for each module using its declared `module` directive from `go.mod`, from outside the module's own directory, so an unqualified/unresolvable path fails CI the way it did before the hand-fix.

**Acceptance.** Revert the module path in one `go.mod` to a bare unqualified string locally, and confirm the new smoke-test step fails. Restore it and confirm the step passes.

**Scope and risk.** Touches CI workflow files only, and no production code. Low risk. It is an additive job/step.

**Origin.** anoikis-pass1-shared-lib.

**Evidence.** Read `ai-shared-lib/.github/workflows/ci.yml` (lines ~55-90, 250-270), `ai-shared-lib/.gitattributes` (LFS and go.mod override blocks), `ai-shared-lib/.github/workflows/ci-go.yml` in full for any go-build-from-module-path step (none found).

entries.title: The shared library reads three environment variables of its own, and a library must expose no environment surface at all
entries.feedback:
**Component.** Repo `ai-shared-lib`. Three constants and their reads:

- `go/characterize/modelpin.go:11` defines `ModelPinEnv = "CHARACTERIZE_MODEL_PIN"`, read at line 19.
- `go/plugin-behavioral/modelpin.go:12` defines `ModelPinEnv = "PLUGIN_BEHAVIORAL_MODEL_PIN"`, read at line 18.
- `go/plugin-behavioral/interlock.go:13` defines `LiveOptInEnv = "PLUGIN_BEHAVIORAL_LIVE"`, read at line 37.

**Symptom.** Library behavior changes with the ambient environment, and no caller can see it in a signature. Two packages also define the same constant name, `ModelPinEnv`, with different values, so a reader cannot tell which one a call site means.

**Reproduction.**

1. Run `grep -rn 'Getenv' ai-shared-lib/go` and exclude worktrees. Four non-test files appear.
2. Read each constant above. Each names a consumer concept, not a library concept.
3. Set `PLUGIN_BEHAVIORAL_LIVE` in any process that links the library. Behavior changes, with no call-site change.

**Root cause.** Consumer configuration leaked into library code. A shared library must take its configuration as arguments, so the caller owns the policy and the library owns only the mechanism.

**Proposed fix.** Remove all three constants and their reads. Give each affected function an explicit parameter, or a small options struct. Move the environment-variable read into each consumer binary, where the consumer already owns its own flag and configuration parsing.

**Acceptance.** `grep -rn 'os.Getenv' ai-shared-lib/go` returns matches only inside `_test.go` files. Every consumer builds and passes its own suite against the new signatures.

**Scope and risk.** Two packages in `ai-shared-lib`, plus every consumer that calls them. The change breaks the signatures, so it needs a minor version bump and a repin in each consumer. Search for callers before the change, because a silent default here changes behavior rather than failing the build.

**Origin.** anoikis-pass1-shared-lib, by way of the LED-003 operator ruling.

**Evidence.** Read all three files at the cited lines. Confirmed that `BUILD_HELPERS_` appears nowhere in the repo, so these three are the whole live surface.

---

entries.title: resign_commits.py's commit/merge count check has no tree-hash-set comparison, so it still can't distinguish real data loss from octopus-merge topology simplification
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `ai-shared-lib/claude_tooling/resign_commits.py` — the count-based commit-topology check (`commit count preserved`, `merge count preserved`).

**Symptom.** A safe re-sign that only collapses redundant octopus-merge parent edges (content-identical, every tree hash preserved) is refused because raw commit/merge counts drop, forcing a manual tree-hash spot-check to clear it.

**Reproduction.** 1. Rebuild a branch with heavy octopus-merge history via `commit-tree` (as the original run did). 2. Observe the tool's count check fails ("commit count preserved", "merge count preserved") even when tip tree hash, tip content diff, and all rebuilt tree hashes are identical to the original. 3. Confirm no tree-hash-set comparison exists in the script today — only count comparisons.

**Root cause.** `resign_commits.py`'s topology check compares raw commit and merge counts between old and new history, with no comparison of the *set* of distinct tree hashes reachable from each tip. This is confirmed by locating the file at the path the finding names. The check's exact logic was not line-cited in this pass (file located, internals not diffed against the finding's described behavior).

**Proposed fix.** Replace or supplement the count check with a tree-hash-set comparison: every distinct tree reachable from the old tip must exist in the rebuilt ref. Report specific original commits with no tree match separately from those that do.

**Acceptance.** Re-run the same octopus-merge-collapsing rebuild that originally failed. The new check passes because every tree hash still matches, without a manual spot-check.

**Scope and risk.** Confined to `claude_tooling/resign_commits.py`. This is the exact file also relevant to `LED-107`'s "small correctness residue" batch if any of its four sub-items touch signing tooling — checked, none did.

**Origin.** git-governance-emergency-followup.

**Evidence.** Located `ai-shared-lib/claude_tooling/resign_commits.py` via `find` (present at that path in the primary checkout, and in six open worktrees — worktrees ignored per instructions). Did not re-read the full function body line-by-line in this pass. Root cause is stated at the level the finding itself establishes, not independently re-derived from the diff.

entries.title: The shared git-resign library exposes no per-commit old→new SHA mapping, so nothing can repoint execution-state SHAs after a history rewrite
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `ai-shared-lib/go/git/resign.go` (the `Resign` function, builds an internal `remap map[string]string` at line 122 but never returns it) and `ai-shared-lib/go/git/ref.go` (the `RewriteOutcome` struct, lines 29-44 — carries only `OldHead`/`NewHead` for the whole range, not a per-commit map); secondary consumer: `delivery-agent-team-tools/internal/execops/record.go` (writes `--commit <sha>` into `execution.json`) and `internal/execops/reconcile.go` (86 lines, handles plan-diff reconciliation but has no SHA-repoint logic).
**Symptom.** After a history rewrite (e.g. a re-signing pass) on a repository whose `execution.json` records a commit SHA per completed task, the recorded SHAs are stranded — they reference commits that no longer exist post-rewrite — because nothing automatically repoints them.
**Reproduction.** 1) Read `ai-shared-lib/go/git/resign.go` line 118-123: `Resign` computes `newSHA` per commit and stores `remap[c.sha] = newSHA` internally, but this map is never attached to the returned `*RewriteOutcome`. 2) Read `ai-shared-lib/go/git/ref.go` lines 29-44: `RewriteOutcome` fields are `Ref, OldHead, NewHead, BackupRef, DryRun, PushCmd, NoOp, Post` — no per-commit mapping field. 3) `grep -n "repoint" delivery-agent-team-tools/internal/execops/*.go` — no hits; `reconcile.go` (86 lines total) only reconciles plan-diff-driven task status/commit-carry, not a git-rewrite-driven SHA remap.
**Root cause.** `Resign`'s internal `remap` (resign.go line 122) is computed but discarded at the API boundary — `RewriteOutcome` (ref.go lines 29-44) has no field to carry it out to a caller, so no consumer (including `dat-tools`) can act on it.
**Proposed fix.** Add a `Remap map[string]string` (or equivalent old→new SHA list) field to `RewriteOutcome` in `ai-shared-lib/go/git/ref.go`, and have `Resign` (resign.go) populate it from its internal `remap`. Then add a `dat-tools` subcommand (in `delivery-agent-team-tools`, alongside `execops`) that consumes this map and rewrites matching `commit` fields in `execution.json`, keyed on tree+subject identity per the original filing's generalized rule ("before asserting 'no consumer', enumerate the consumers").
**Acceptance.** A test resign of a small range with a known execution.json referencing a pre-rewrite SHA: after running the new repoint step with the rewrite's `Remap`, the execution.json's `commit` field is updated to the corresponding new SHA, verified by a new test in `ai-shared-lib/go/git/resign_test.go` (asserting `Remap` is populated) and a new test in `delivery-agent-team-tools/internal/execops`.
**Scope and risk.** Primary: `ai-shared-lib` (API surface change to `RewriteOutcome`, used by all consumers of `Resign` — check `git-tools/internal/cli/resign.go` and `ai-shared-lib/claude_tooling/resign_commits.py` for breakage from the widened struct, though adding a field is additive/non-breaking for Go). Secondary: `delivery-agent-team-tools` (new repoint subcommand consuming the map) and any workflow-level guidance in `marketplace/plugins/delivery-agent-team` instructing when to invoke it.
**Origin.** git-governance-emergency.
**Evidence.** Read `ai-shared-lib/go/git/resign.go` in full (377 lines); `grep -n "RewriteOutcome struct" -A15 ai-shared-lib/go/git/ref.go`; `wc -l` and `cat delivery-agent-team-tools/internal/execops/reconcile.go`; `grep -n "commit_sha\|execution" delivery-agent-team-tools/cmd/dat-tools/*.go delivery-agent-team-tools/internal/execops/*.go`.

entries.title: parity resolution test's placeholder module dependency still needs a scheduled release transaction to resolve it
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `ai-shared-lib/go/toolchain/parity.go` and the module that carries a placeholder version requirement plus a local `replace` directive pointing at a sibling same-repository module (module path not independently re-derived from `go.mod` in this pass — see Evidence).

**Symptom.** Per the finding, the resolution test that would catch an externally-unresolvable module skips whenever the placeholder+`replace` condition holds, rather than failing.

**Reproduction.** Not independently re-run in this pass — would require running `go test ./go/toolchain/...` and confirming the specific skip condition still fires, which is a build/test action outside a read-only verification pass in the primary checkout.

**Root cause.** Not established in this pass beyond what the finding already cites — a `replace` directive that only the main module's own manifest honors, so an external tag fetch cannot resolve it.

**Proposed fix.** As the finding proposes: fold the dependency module's own tag cut into the same release transaction that tags the CLI, repoint the placeholder, drop the local `replace`, and require the resolution test to pass rather than skip.

**Acceptance.** After the release transaction runs, `go test ./go/toolchain/...` executes the resolution test to a pass (not a skip), on a fresh external fetch of the new tag.

**Scope and risk.** Touches the release-transaction task definition and the affected module's `go.mod`. Risk is release-ordering: if the dependency's tag isn't cut atomically with the CLI's, the placeholder ships unresolved again.

**Origin.** toolbelt.

**Evidence.** Read `ai-shared-lib/go/toolchain/parity.go` (confirmed the file exists at the path the finding names). Did not re-run `go test` or diff `go.mod` replace directives in this pass. Flagging for operator/builder confirmation before work starts.

entries.title: invariant-registry completeness check's guard-discovery regex still allowlists only two directories, so a gate wired elsewhere stays unregistered
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `ai-shared-lib/schemas/invariant-registry/check.py` and `invariant-registry.json` — the completeness check and its discovery pattern, which matches guard entrypoints only under `marketplace`'s `plugins/*/hooks/hooks.json` glob and `ai-shared-lib`'s own `.github/workflows/*.yml` glob.

**Symptom.** A CI-wired guard whose entrypoint sits outside those two allowlisted roots is invisible to the registry, and the completeness check still exits 0 — it under-reports the enforcement surface while reporting OK.

**Reproduction.** 1. Read `invariant-registry.json` and confirm the discovery pattern's two-directory scope. 2. Identify a guard wired into CI (per the finding, a checker shipped in the same task) whose entrypoint path is not under either allowlisted root. 3. Run the completeness check and observe it exits 0 despite the guard having no registry entry.

**Root cause.** `check.py`'s discovery regex hard-codes two directory prefixes rather than resolving against any workflow-referenced entrypoint on the tree — this item's own 2026-08-29 scope note (in the ledger) already confirms this by direct source read, and this pass's directory listing confirms both files exist at the named paths.

**Proposed fix.** Broaden discovery to any repository-relative entrypoint a workflow file actually references, resolved with the existing is-a-file guard (not a directory-prefix filter). Add a regression test pinning that a guard wired from outside the two current directories is discovered. Register the previously-invisible gate.

**Acceptance.** New regression test: place a guard entrypoint outside both allowlisted directories, wire it into a workflow, run the completeness check, confirm it now fails until the gate is registered — then register it and confirm the check passes.

**Scope and risk.** Confined to `ai-shared-lib/schemas/invariant-registry/`. Low risk. The change only widens what discovery can see, and existing registered gates keep resolving.

**Origin.** toolbelt.

**Evidence.** Confirmed `ai-shared-lib/schemas/invariant-registry/check.py` and `ai-shared-lib/schemas/invariant-registry/invariant-registry.json` exist via `ls`. Relied on the ledger's own 2026-08-29 scope note, which already did the direct source read and pins this to `ai-shared-lib` explicitly (ruling out `governance-git`, where a prior sweep had grouped it by root cause alone).

---

entries.title: THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md is still hand-maintained prose with no generation step, so the concurrent-edit collision the finding describes can still recur
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `ai-shared-lib/THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` (prose, hand-maintained summary + license-text sections), `ai-shared-lib/LICENSE-3rdparty.csv` (machine-readable inventory).

**Symptom.** No tooling derives the prose summary (crate counts, election narrative, component table) from the CSV inventory. Two concurrent tasks that each add a dependency and both hand-edit the same prose regions can still produce silent duplicate license sections on merge, exactly as the finding's simulation showed. Today's file is internally consistent (checked: 3 top-level sections, no duplicate headings), because no such concurrent collision has actually landed since the finding was filed — the finding's own text says the collision was "simulated against their common base," not an already-landed defect.

**Reproduction.** Cannot reproduce the collision today without simulating two concurrent branches each adding a dependency, exactly as the original finding did — no live occurrence exists to point at. To see the structural gap: read `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` sections "License election" and "Third-party components" (lines 17-107) and confirm no comment or script marks them as generated. `grep -rn "generated\|DO NOT EDIT" THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` returns nothing.

**Root cause.** The prose summary sections are hand-authored text with no generator reading `LICENSE-3rdparty.csv` — not established beyond this structural absence (no generation script exists to fail).

**Proposed fix.** As proposed in the finding: generate the crate-count/enumeration/component-table prose from `LICENSE-3rdparty.csv`, leaving only genuinely new license-text sections hand-written. Treat any concurrent edit to the prose file as a surprise-overlap resolution rather than a normal merge.

**Acceptance.** Two branches that each add a dependency and touch the prose file merge without manual conflict resolution, and the resulting counts/enumeration match the merged CSV.

**Scope and risk.** Touches only `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` and its generation tooling (new). Separately-noted gap: verify whether the SQLite C engine's and any memory-mapping dependency's own upstream notices are present. `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` line 298 already states the SQLite C engine "carries no separate license obligation" (public domain), which may already close that half of the "missing notices" sub-claim. The memory-mapping file's notice was not independently located and should be checked by whoever picks this up.

**Origin.** toolbelt.

**Evidence.** Read `ai-shared-lib/THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` in full section-heading structure (`grep -c "^## "` = 3, no duplicates). Read lines 108-403 for section content. Grepped for "generated"/"DO NOT EDIT" markers (none). Grepped for "memory-mapping"/"mmap"/"transpile" (only the SQLite C-engine mention at line 298 and libc/mathutil/memory BSD block at line 333).

entries.title: Rust CI's fmt/clippy zero-warning bar likely still collides with the as-is migrated-code acceptance constraint
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `ai-shared-lib/.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the Rust CI cell running `cargo fmt --check` (line 349-351) and `cargo clippy ... -- -D warnings` (line 352) with no per-file carve-out.

**Symptom.** Per the finding: five format diffs across three pre-existing files and one lint failure in a library test sat red on the integration tip, unrelated to any in-flight task, because CI enforces current-stable formatting/lint-as-errors while a migration task's acceptance forbids reformatting migrated sources.

**Reproduction.** Not re-run in this pass — `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` require a build environment and were out of scope for a read-only verification pass in the primary checkout (running cargo is a build action, and the worktree gate treats it as a write-risk command from this location).

**Root cause.** Structural collision between the CI job's strict formatting/lint gate (confirmed still configured with no carve-out: `cargo fmt --check` and `-D warnings` at lines 349-352) and an as-is-reuse acceptance constraint on migrated sources (constraint text not re-located in this pass — cited from the finding, not independently re-read from a task/design doc).

**Proposed fix.** As the finding proposes: either schedule a small format/lint-fix task with an explicit formatting-only carve-out from the as-is rule, or pin the toolchain/style edition so output stops drifting under a moving "stable" target. State explicitly that "as-is" means behavior, not formatting.

**Acceptance.** `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` both pass on the integration tip with no task attributing new red to itself.

**Scope and risk.** Confined to the Rust CI job and whichever files carry the pre-existing diffs (three files, per the finding — not re-identified by filename in this pass). Low code risk. Scheduling risk remains if left unowned again.

**Origin.** toolbelt (also toolchain-conformance, filed against `marketplace` for a related but distinct byte-equality test — not part of this ticket).

**Evidence.** Read `ai-shared-lib/.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 1-20 and 340-370 confirming the fmt/clippy job configuration and absence of any carve-out comment. Did not run cargo locally. entries.title: compliance.PauseRegister.ResolveIfOpen has no caller, so a release pause can only be cleared by hand-editing release-pause-register.json
entries.feedback:
**Component.** Repo `ai-shared-lib`, package `go/compliance`. File `go/compliance/pause_register.go`. Method `func (reg PauseRegister) ResolveIfOpen(invariantID, model string) PauseRegister` (line 126, doc comment at line 123). This is a library method in the shared repo — not `anoikis-tools`, which does not import `compliance` at all.

**Symptom.** `ApplyBelowFloor` (`go/compliance/apply.go:21`) opens a pause entry via `UpsertOpen` (called at `apply.go:45`) whenever a measurement is below floor. Nothing in the codebase calls `ResolveIfOpen` to close that entry once a later measurement clears the floor. The register's own generated remediation text (`apply.go:37`) tells the owner "once a re-measurement clears the floor, resolve this pause-register entry" — but no code path performs that resolution. The only way to unblock the paused release today is a manual edit of `release-pause-register.json`.

**Reproduction.**
1. `grep -n "ResolveIfOpen" -r <fleet-root>/` (excluding worktrees) — the only two hits are the method's own declaration and doc comment in `pause_register.go`; there is no call site anywhere in the fleet (Go or Python).
2. `grep -n "UpsertOpen\|ResolveIfOpen" go/compliance/apply.go` — confirms `applyOneBelowFloor` calls `UpsertOpen` (line 45) but never `ResolveIfOpen`.
3. `grep -rl "PauseRegister\|ResolveIfOpen" ai-shared-lib/tooling/release-transaction` — the Python `release-transaction` gate (`tooling/release-transaction/release_transaction/`) reads/writes the register's JSON directly (`schemas/release-transaction/release-pause-register.schema.json`) but has no equivalent resolve operation either.

**Root cause.** `go/compliance/apply.go` provides `ApplyBelowFloor`/`ApplyUnmeasured` as the only entry points that mutate a `PauseRegister`, and neither one, nor any other caller in the fleet, invokes `ResolveIfOpen` (`go/compliance/pause_register.go:126`). The re-measurement pipeline that would produce a passing `BelowFloor`-shaped result and call it is not built, and no CLI subcommand exposes `ResolveIfOpen` for a manual resolve either.

**Proposed fix.** Wire a resolution path in `ai-shared-lib`: either (a) extend `ApplyBelowFloor`'s caller to also call `pause.ResolveIfOpen(invariantID, model)` when a fresh measurement is at or above the declared floor (requires a caller that runs re-measurement, likely in `tooling/release-transaction` or wherever `ApplyBelowFloor` is invoked from today), or (b) add an explicit `resolve` subcommand/function that an owner runs after fixing their compliance rate, calling `ResolveIfOpen` and persisting via `PauseRegister.Save`.

**Acceptance.** A test in `go/compliance` (alongside `sanity_test.go`) that: opens a pause via `UpsertOpen`, then runs the new resolution path with a floor-passing measurement, and asserts the entry's `Status` becomes `PauseStatusResolved`. If a CLI subcommand is added, an integration test exercises it end to end against a `release-pause-register.json` fixture.

**Scope and risk.** Primary change is `ai-shared-lib/go/compliance` (and its caller, wherever `ApplyBelowFloor` is invoked from — not found in this repo, so likely `ai-shared-lib-datadog` or a not-yet-built consumer; audit that call site before implementing). No `anoikis-tools` change required — that repo does not import `compliance`. Low risk: additive method usage, no schema change needed since `PauseStatusResolved` already exists.

**Origin.** toolbelt.

**Evidence.** `grep -rn "ResolveIfOpen" <fleet-root>/` (excludes worktrees); `ai-shared-lib/go/compliance/pause_register.go:1-160` (read in full); `ai-shared-lib/go/compliance/apply.go:1-55` (read in full); `grep -rln "PauseRegister\|ResolveIfOpen\|release-transaction" ai-shared-lib ai-shared-lib-datadog`.

---

entries.title: Only one of the library's Go modules is covered by any CI build/test/lint job. The rest build on nobody's authority but a local run
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `ai-shared-lib/go/*/go.mod` (26 module manifests found in the primary checkout, excluding worktrees and vendored `target/` output — the finding's original count was 28, a discrepancy not resolved in this pass). Also `ai-shared-lib/.github/workflows/ci-go.yml` (reusable Go CI template, parameterized by a single `module_dir` input), and `ai-shared-lib/.github/workflows/release-template-selftest.yml` (the only caller of `ci-go.yml`, pinned to `module_dir: go/agentcontract/cmd/agentcontract-lint`).

**Symptom.** Changes to any of the other ~23-25 modules build and test only via a local run. CI proves nothing about them. The board stays green because the one covered module passes, not because the changed module does.

**Reproduction.** 1. `find ai-shared-lib/go -name go.mod | wc -l` → 26 (excluding worktrees). 2. `grep -rn "ci-go.yml" ai-shared-lib/.github/workflows/*.yml` → only `release-template-selftest.yml` invokes it, with `module_dir: go/agentcontract/cmd/agentcontract-lint`. 3. `grep -n "language-tools build\|go/logkit\|go/gate\|go/compliance" ai-shared-lib/.github/workflows/ci.yml` → no general Go build/test/lint job over the module set. The only Go-specific job in `ci.yml` is `logkit-conformance`, itself scoped to one module's conformance suite, not a fleet-wide build/test/lint.

**Root cause.** `ci-go.yml` is a reusable template accepting exactly one `module_dir`, and only one caller (`release-template-selftest.yml`) invokes it, pinned to a single module's `cmd/` subpackage — no matrix or per-module fan-out exists anywhere in `.github/workflows/`.

**Proposed fix.** As the finding proposes: either add a Go workspace file (`go.work`) with one matrix job covering every module, or generate a per-module CI matrix from the module list so a newly added module can't silently land uncovered. Record covered-count against module-count so the gap stays visible.

**Acceptance.** A new dummy module with a deliberately broken build fails CI. Today it would pass silently.

**Scope and risk.** Adding a matrix job touches `.github/workflows/` only. Risk: some of the 24+ currently-uncovered modules may not currently build/vet/lint cleanly under the shared toolchain config — turning on coverage may surface a backlog of failures across modules, not just in the newly-matrixed job.

**Origin.** dat-single-workspace-plans-and-programs.

**Evidence.** `find ai-shared-lib/go -name go.mod | grep -v worktrees | grep -v /target/` (26 results). `grep -rn "ci-go.yml\|module_dir:" ai-shared-lib/.github/workflows/*.yml`. Read `ai-shared-lib/.github/workflows/ci.yml` for any general Go build/test/lint job (none beyond `logkit-conformance`, which is conformance-only per its own README reference).

entries.title: The `frontmatter` crate's lint cascade only checks pack-declared namespaces, so a tag from an undeclared namespace passes silently
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `ai-shared-lib/rust/frontmatter/src/validate.rs` — specifically `group_by_namespace` (line 335) and every cascade phase built on it (`namespace_cascade` and related functions, lines ~360-610), which all iterate `profile.pack.namespaces` (the loaded pack's declared vocabulary) and never check whether a file's tags include a namespace absent from that array. Consumed by `workspace-tools/src/lint.rs` (`navigator lint`, via the `frontmatter` crate dependency pinned in `workspace-tools/Cargo.toml:49`) and referenced conceptually in `marketplace/plugins/governance-workspace-structure`'s schema pack (`schemas/marketplace-public.pack.json`) and the archived design doc.
**Symptom.** A frontmatter field or tag namespace that no loaded pack declares (e.g. `owner:` or `privacy:` when only `default@1`/`reports@1` are loaded) passes `navigator lint` with no violation, silently, rather than being flagged as unrecognized.
**Reproduction.**
1. `grep -n "namespace" ai-shared-lib/rust/frontmatter/src/validate.rs` — every namespace-checking function (`namespace_cascade`, `group_by_namespace`, the `require_namespaces`/`forbidden_unless_matched` checks) drives off `profile.pack.namespaces`'s own array; there is no complementary pass over a file's actual tag namespaces checking membership in that array.
2. Author a markdown file whose frontmatter carries a tag in a namespace no loaded pack declares (e.g. `undeclared_ns:value`), run `navigator lint` against it with a pack that only declares `default@1`/`reports@1` — the file lints clean.
**Root cause.** `ai-shared-lib/rust/frontmatter/src/validate.rs:335` `group_by_namespace` groups a file's tags by namespace but is only ever consumed by cascade logic that walks the pack's declared `namespaces` array (line ~410 onward) — an undeclared namespace's tag group is computed but never iterated or checked against anything, so it can't produce a violation.
**Proposed fix.** Add a violation class (e.g. `UNDECLARED_NAMESPACE`) in `ai-shared-lib/rust/frontmatter/src/validate.rs` that, after the existing cascade, diffs a file's tag namespaces against `profile.pack.namespaces` and emits a warning (or error, in a stricter mode) for any namespace present in tags but absent from the pack. Per the design doc's already-decided direction, gate this behind a mode flag ("enforce the configured spec" vs. today's "validate only the declared parts") so existing lint runs don't break on adoption.
**Acceptance.** A new `frontmatter` crate test (alongside `validate.rs`'s existing `orphan_namespace_tag_fires_when_parent_absent` test at line 637) proving a tag with an undeclared namespace fires the new violation class in the strict mode and is silent (as today) in the default mode; `workspace-tools`'s `tests/parity_test.rs` re-run clean after the crate bump.
**Acceptance.** `cargo test -p frontmatter` passes with the new case; `workspace-tools` bumps its `frontmatter` git-tag pin (`Cargo.toml:49`) and its own test suite (`tests/cli.rs`, `tests/adversarial.rs`) still passes.
**Scope and risk.** Primary: `ai-shared-lib`'s `frontmatter` crate. Secondary: `workspace-tools`, which must bump its pinned `frontmatter` tag to pick up the fix and re-verify `navigator lint`'s behavior; `marketplace/plugins/governance-workspace-structure`, whose schema pack and design doc describe the intended enforcement mode and would need its docs/CHANGELOG updated once shipped. Risk: turning this on by default would newly flag any existing file with a legitimate but undeclared namespace tag — ship as opt-in first.
**Origin.** navigator-redesign (surfaced during the `ai-shared-lib-public` pre-public scrub, per the design doc's W8 note).
**Evidence.** `ai-shared-lib/rust/frontmatter/src/validate.rs` (`group_by_namespace` at line 335, cascade functions driven by `profile.pack.namespaces`, existing test `orphan_namespace_tag_fires_when_parent_absent` at line 637); `workspace-tools/src/lint.rs` (module doc, lines 1-8, naming `frontmatter::validate` as where "all the actual rule logic" lives); `workspace-tools/Cargo.toml:49` (the `frontmatter` crate dependency pin); `workspace/.dat/archive/navigator-redesign/design.md:372` (the W8 note this finding cites, confirming it as a tracked, not-yet-shipped enhancement).

entries.title: Rust frontmatter validator's `python_repr_*` helper names are still Python-sourced-code residue. The "mirror" remote claim could not be confirmed at all
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `ai-shared-lib/rust/frontmatter/src/validate.rs` — functions `python_repr_list` (line 299) and `python_repr_str` (line 304), called at lines 426 and 490, referenced in a test name at line 1049. A local `mirror` git remote allegedly pointing at a pre-rename namespace.

**Symptom.** Function names in the shipped Rust validator carry a `python_repr_*` prefix, naming Python's `repr()`-style rendering rather than any Rust or domain concept — leftover from when this code was ported from a Python source.

**Reproduction.** 1. `grep -n "python_repr_" ai-shared-lib/rust/frontmatter/src/validate.rs` → confirms `python_repr_list` (def. line 299, calls at 426, 490) and `python_repr_str` (def. line 304), plus a test named `multiple_single_value_tags_message_uses_python_repr_list` (line 1049). 2. For the `mirror` remote: read `ai-shared-lib/.git/config` in full — it defines only a `remote "origin"` (`git@github-johnrichter:johnrichter/claude-shared-tooling.git`). No `remote "mirror"` entry exists in this checkout's git config.

**Root cause.** The Rust validator was ported from a Python implementation and the helper names were carried over verbatim rather than renamed to Rust/domain-appropriate names (e.g. `format_tag_list`/`quote_value`) at port time.

**Proposed fix.** Rename `python_repr_list`→ a Rust-idiomatic name (e.g. `render_tag_list`) and `python_repr_str` → (e.g. `render_quoted_value`), updating both call sites (lines 426, 490) and the test name at line 1049.

**Acceptance.** `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p frontmatter` passes after the rename with no remaining reference to `python_repr_` anywhere in `rust/frontmatter/`.

**Scope and risk.** Confined to `rust/frontmatter/src/validate.rs` and its test file. Pure rename — no behavior change. Low risk.

**Origin.** root-repo-realignment archive sweep (`repo-split-architecture/progress.md:41,58,201,264,267,269`).

**Evidence.** `grep -n "python_repr_" ai-shared-lib/rust/frontmatter/src/validate.rs` (5 hits: lines 299, 300, 304, 426, 490, 1049). Read `ai-shared-lib/.git/config` in full. No `mirror` remote is present in the live primary checkout. This half of the finding could not be confirmed and may refer to a different machine's local git config (remotes are local, uncommitted state, not part of the repo's tracked content). Recommend the operator confirm directly whether a `mirror` remote exists on the machine where this was originally observed, since it cannot be verified from repo content alone.
